forms.frenchAnswer: Sam salue la barista Rosa à Oaxaca : Bonjour !
forms.englishPrompt: Sam greets the barista Rosa in Oaxaca: Good morning!
forms.explanation: Salue = greets. Oaxaca stays as the place name. Bonjour is the French greeting used for Good morning.

forms.frenchAnswer: Sam lit la carte et commande un jus d'orange.
forms.englishPrompt: Sam reads the menu and orders an orange juice.
forms.explanation: Lit = reads; commande = orders. La carte is the menu you read from; le menu usually means a fixed-price set menu. Jus d'orange = orange juice.

forms.frenchAnswer: Pour manger, Sam commande des œufs avec des tortillas mexicaines.
forms.englishPrompt: To eat, Sam orders eggs with tortillas.
forms.explanation: Des means some (plural); tortilla mexicaine identifies the Mexican flatbread in this Oaxaca scene, since tortilla alone in French can mean a Spanish omelette.

forms.frenchAnswer: Rosa recommande un churro et du pain sucré.
forms.englishPrompt: Rosa recommends a churro and sweet bread.
forms.explanation: Churro is kept as a loan word. Du = some (masculine). Pain sucré renders sweet bread and stands for Mexican pan dulce.

forms.englishPrompt: Sam: Thank you very much, see you tomorrow!
forms.explanation: Merci beaucoup = thank you very much; à demain = see you tomorrow.

sourceNotes: The contextual qualifier mexicaine disambiguates the source tortilla from a Spanish omelette; it does not substitute another food.
Every noun card carries its definite article to match the English 'the'.
Rosa's greeting stays formal (vous) because the Spanish source uses usted and the card note marks it formal.
La barista is feminine because the Spanish source says 'la barista Rosa'.
Sam's gender is not stated in the source, so the card and Reader show enchanté(e); no type, write or say target uses that line.
Sweet bread is rendered pain sucré for the source's pan dulce.
Recall, type and say use exact source card pairs; see, hear and write use exact Reader pairs.
Hear mode is partner/script only; no recorded audio is claimed.
The Spanish pronunciation and usage notes on the source cards are not carried into French.
Unreviewed owner-only draft. Review, audio and learner gates remain closed; no approval of any kind is claimed.
qualifiedReviewResiduals: Gates: review, audio and learner gates all remain closed. This is an unreviewed owner-only draft and nothing here is an approval, qualified or otherwise.

Sam's gender: the owner must decide between enchanté and enchantée, or choose an invariant wording such as 'c'est un plaisir'. Until then, any grader must accept both spellings for the card and Reader line 3.
Tortilla: 'la tortilla' can also mean a Spanish omelette in French. The owner may prefer 'la tortilla mexicaine' or 'la tortilla de maïs' at the cost of exact parity with the source.
Bonjour renders both 'Good morning!' and the 'Hi' in Rosa's line. This is deliberate, to keep the formal usted register, and needs owner confirmation.
Pain sucré is a literal rendering of pan dulce. The owner should confirm it or choose another term.
'Au revoir, bonne journée.' does not show the formality that 'que le vaya bien' marks with usted. It is polite and register-neutral; the owner should confirm that is enough.

Source card notes are Spanish-specific (pronunciation of café, jugo, leche, ll, rr, silent h; 'buenas tardes' after noon). They were not translated, and no French pronunciation or usage notes were written.
The goodbye card still has no Reader line. Its only practice is the say mode, because Reader content was not invented.
Exact-pair rule: recall, type and say now use card pairs, not Reader pairs. If the pipeline accepts only Reader pairs, these three modes need reworking and the label problem returns.
Typography: the French strings use a space before '!', '?' and ':'. Typed-answer grading should normalise that spacing, apostrophes and the œ ligature.
Level scope: formal vous, du/des and 'ne… pas de' appear in the Reader. The owner should confirm these are in scope for Foundation 1.
No audio exists. Hear mode is partner-read from the script only.
This adjudication was done read-only without tools. Nothing was checked against repository files or validators.
